subject: Close runway tension - MAP rewrite & contingency ask
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Close runway tension - MAP rewrite & contingency ask

Team —

Quick internal note before we surface this to ScaleHealth: their acceptance window has slipped by ~10 business days due to a delayed procurement approval and an extra SOC2 evidence review. That puts our previously agreed go-live at risk and shrinks the margin for the canary rollout.

I sketched an updated MAP (see draft attached MAP_v2.xlsx) with three levers: a trimmed pilot scope, a staged acceptance cadence (week-by-week rather than all at once), and a fallback execution path that routes lower-critical traffic to our hosted variant while we complete Dedicated onboarding.

Please do the following by EOD today:
- Ben: send the external note to procurement and ops with the updated MAP and ask for a committed procurement date.
- Jordan: confirm which features we can trim for the pilot without jeopardizing the customer's acceptance criteria.
- Marissa: validate the SLA/credit language we might need if go-live slips again (I know we've had similar language in DEV-templates).

Attachments referenced: MAP_v2.xlsx (draft), SOC2_evidence_request.pdf (customer request pdf).

Goal is to get a single committed procurement date and an acknowledgement of the staggered acceptance approach so we can rebaseline the timeline and avoid a last-minute credit ask.

Thanks —
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Michael O'Rourke <michael@scalehealth.com>, ScaleHealth Procurement <procurement@scalehealth.com>, Ops Lead <ops@scalehealth.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Close runway tension - MAP rewrite & contingency ask

Michael / team —

Following up from our call this morning: thanks for the transparency on procurement timing. We captured the options discussed and proposed a short MAP in the attached workbook (MAP_v2.xlsx). Summary:

- Staged acceptance: week 1 = API validation + small internal cohort; week 2 = expanded integration tests; week 3 = production ramp to 20% traffic.
- Pilot trim: defer advanced reranking and long-context evaluation to phase 2 to shorten validation time.
- Fallback: if Reserved Dedicated capacity isn't ready by the agreed cutover, we can temporarily route traffic to our hosted API plus a prefix cache to preserve latency while we finish Dedicated provisioning.

Can you confirm two things by COB Mon, Apr 5:
1) A committed procurement approval date (calendar day),
2) That the staged acceptance approach is acceptable to your validation/QA team (if not, please list the minimum feature set you require for week 1).

If procurement is delayed beyond Apr 15, we should escalate to the account steering committee and discuss short-term credits to cover the extended test window.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: MAP_v2.xlsx

From: Ops Lead <ops@scalehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: ScaleHealth Procurement <procurement@scalehealth.com>, Michael O'Rourke <michael@scalehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Close runway tension - MAP rewrite & contingency ask

Ben / Naomi —

Thanks for the clear plan and the staged approach — that helps. Short answers for what you asked:

1) Procurement: we have an internal procurement approval meeting scheduled for Apr 12. Procurement team expects sign-off by Apr 14 assuming no additional evidence items.

2) QA validation: staged acceptance is acceptable. For week 1 we need: authentication + tokenization work, embedding parity check, and a focused run of our 200-step integration harness. Reranking and long-context are allowed to be deferred.

Note: Procurement also flagged an outstanding SOC2 evidence item (they attached a question list) which could add 3–5 business days if they request additional artefacts. We attached the list here.

-Mike (on behalf of Ops)

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Close runway tension - MAP rewrite & contingency ask

Michael / procurement team —

Appreciate the quick reply and the clarity on the QA minimum for week 1. Per Ops' note, we will:

- Update the MAP to explicitly show the week-by-week acceptance checklist (attached MAP_v2.xlsx, tab "Acceptance Plan").
- Mark the SOC2 evidence item as high impact and include a conformance checklist; we attached the customer-provided questions and our suggested artefacts (SOC2_evidence_request.pdf).
- Confirm a fallback routing plan: if Dedicated provisioning misses the cutover we will run two weeks on hosted+cache, with an agreed credit formula if that extension exceeds 10 business days.

Ask: please confirm procurement approval by Apr 14 if feasible. If there is any expectation procurement may ask additional artefacts beyond what we've attached, flag it now so we can pre-assign owners (Marissa will own contractual language, Jordan will own the pilot-scope trim list).

Related links: HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/deals/7843) and the working MAP folder (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_MAP_rewrite).

If procurement confirms Apr 14 we will rebaseline the go-live target to Apr 29 and circulate an updated timeline and canary plan to the exec steering committee. If procurement cannot commit, we will request a short-term credit conversation and set an internal escalations call for Tue Apr 6.

Best —
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachment: MAP_v2.xlsx, SOC2_evidence_request.pdf
